sections.content: How many people stayed in East Cowes after gaining qualifications?

East Cowes is a small town in the South East. East Cowes does not have its own university.

East Cowes has higher levels of deprivation.

Overall, East Cowes ended up with:

  • fewer non-graduates with advanced qualifications than it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

In East Cowes, 350 state school pupils sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 2011 school years.

Of these, 55 (16%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as definied by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 130 (37%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare East Cowes to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of East Cowes' pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in East Cowes in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there in 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, all affected students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left East Cowes move to?

Of East Cowes's qualified non-graduates, 65 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 45 of those (69%) were living fairly locally, in the Isle of Wight travel to work area (TTWA).

In 2018 to 2019, 48% of qualified non-graduates living in East Cowes had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 115 qualified non-graduates from our cohort living in East Cowes, compared with the 130 qualified non-graduates who sat their GCSEs there.

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, 52% of qualified non-graduates in East Cowes had sat their GCSEs there, while 48% had moved there from elsewhere.
